problems.memo_sentence: The authors conceptually survey several quantum approaches—quantum optimisation (Adiabatic Algorithm, Quantum Annealing, QAOA), quantum machine learning, and quantum sensors—highlighting their mechanisms and potential roles in energy and finance.
problems.source_evidence: The paper’s literature review cites prior work for these topics, e.g. Table 1 lists references such as Farhi et al. (2000), Ciliberto et al. (2018), Paudel et al. (2022), Orús et al. (2019), and others as the sources of the surveyed methods.
problems.explanation: The memo presents the survey of quantum approaches as if it were the paper’s own conceptual contribution, but the paper is largely summarizing prior literature. This is a wrong attribution because the mechanisms and roles are drawn from cited references rather than newly developed by the authors.

problems.memo_sentence: The authors also claim, citing prior work, that QML-based anomaly detection can reduce false positives in grid monitoring by up to 30% compared with classical ANN models, and argue that quantum optimisation and QML can enhance reliability, accuracy, and precision via high-dimensional learning and amplitude amplification.
problems.source_evidence: In Section III.F the paper says: “For example, a QML-based anomaly detection model reduces false positives in power grid monitoring by up to 30% compared to classical ANN models[8].” The cited reference [8] is W. V. Dam et al., 2021, not a result generated in this paper.
problems.explanation: The memo correctly notes the 30% figure but attributes it to the paper’s own claims rather than to the cited prior study. The source explicitly ties the result to reference [8], so this is a wrong attribution.

problems.memo_sentence: The authors also claim, citing prior work, that QML-based anomaly detection can reduce false positives in grid monitoring by up to 30% compared with classical ANN models, and argue that quantum optimisation and QML can enhance reliability, accuracy, and precision via high-dimensional learning and amplitude amplification.
problems.source_evidence: The same paragraph states: “An experimental benchmark is necessary to draw conclusions about the potential of this technique because the Quantum Annealing returns a solution without any guarantees regarding its quality.”
problems.explanation: The memo mentions the 30% result but omits the nearby caution that QA solutions have no quality guarantees and require experimental benchmarking. That limitation materially qualifies the optimism around the optimization methods discussed in the same section.

problems.memo_sentence: The paper suggests several forward-looking directions: developing hybrid process optimisation schemes, pursuing in-practice deployment of quantum methods on current platforms, and working on generalizing input data.
problems.source_evidence: Section VIII (“OPEN ISSUES”) explicitly states that India has “Uneven Progress,” “Inadequate Pace of Improvement,” and that “Environmental Sustainability” will be extremely difficult, with deforestation, improper energy management, pollution of the air and water, and other factors contributing to the depletion of natural resources.
problems.explanation: The memo captures future directions but does not reflect the paper’s explicit open-issues limitations about uneven progress, slow improvement, and environmental sustainability challenges. These are substantive constraints on the paper’s SDG-7 framing.
